# 1 Chronicles Chapter 19 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 380v

---

**19:1** And-it-was after this, and-died Nachash king of-the-sons of-Ammon, and-reigned his-son in-his-place.

**19:2** And-said David: I-will-do loyalty [chesed] with Chanun son of-Nachash, for his-father did loyalty with-me. And-sent David messengers [mal'akhim] to-comfort-him [lenachamo] concerning his-father. And-came the-servants of-David to the-land of-the-sons of-Ammon, to Chanun, to-comfort-him.

**19:3** And-said the-princes [sarey] of-the-sons of-Ammon to Chanun: Is-David honoring [ha-mekhabbed] your-father in-your-eyes, that he-sent to-you comforters [menachamim]? Is-it-not to-search [lachqor] and-to-overthrow [velahapokh] and-to-spy-out [uleraggel] the-land [that] his-servants have-come to-you?

**19:4** And-took Chanun the-servants of-David and-shaved-them [vayegallechem] and-cut [vayyiqtsots] their-garments [maddeyhem] in-the-middle [ba-chetsi] up-to the-buttocks [ha-mifsa'ah], and-sent-them-away.

**19:5** And-went [people] and-told David concerning the-men, and-he-sent to-meet-them, for the-men were very ashamed [nikhlamu me'od]. And-said the-king: Stay [shevu] in-Yericho until your-beards grow-back [yitsmach], and-[then] return.

**19:6** And-saw the-sons of-Ammon that they-had-made-themselves-odious [hit'ba'ashu] with David, and-sent Chanun and-the-sons of-Ammon a-thousand talents [kikkar] of-silver to-hire for-themselves chariots [rekhev] and-horsemen [parashim] from Aram-Naharayim and-from Aram-Ma'akhah and-from Tsovah.

**19:7** And-they-hired for-themselves thirty-two thousand chariots and the-king of-Ma'akhah and-his-people, and-they-came and-camped before Medva. And-the-sons of-Ammon gathered from-their-cities and-came for-the-battle [la-milchamah].

**19:8** And-heard David, and-he-sent Yo'av and-all the-army of-the-mighty-men [gibbor].

**19:9** And-came-out the-sons of-Ammon and-arranged battle [vayyaa'rekhu milchamah] at-the-entrance of-the-city, and-the-kings who had-come [were] by-themselves in-the-field [ba-sadeh].

**19:10** And-saw Yo'av that the-face of-the-battle was toward-him, before and-behind, and-he-chose from-all the-chosen [mivchar] in-Yisra'el and-arranged [them] to-meet Aram.

**19:11** And-the-rest of-the-people he-gave in-the-hand of-Avshai his-brother, and-they-arranged [themselves] to-meet the-sons of-Ammon.

**19:12** And-he-said: If Aram is-too-strong [techezaq] for-me, then-you-shall-be for-me as-salvation [lishu'ah]; and-if the-sons of-Ammon are-too-strong for-you, then-I-will-save-you [vehoshatiykha].

**19:13** Be-strong [chazaq] and-let-us-be-strong [venitkchazaq] for-our-people and-for the-cities of-our-Elohim, and-YHWH — the-good [ha-tov] in-his-eyes he-will-do.

**19:14** And-drew-near Yo'av and-the-people who [were] with-him before Aram for-the-battle, and-they-fled [vayyanusu] from-before-him.

**19:15** And-the-sons of-Ammon saw that Aram had-fled, and-they-also fled from-before Avshai his-brother, and-they-came the-city. And-came Yo'av to-Yerushalayim.

**19:16** And-saw Aram that they-were-struck before Yisra'el, and-they-sent messengers and-brought-out Aram that [was] from-beyond the-River [ha-nahar], and-Shofakh the-commander of-the-army [sar tseva] of-Hadad'ezer [was] before-them.

**19:17** And-it-was-told to-David, and-he-gathered all Yisra'el and-crossed the-Yarden and-came upon-them and-arranged [battle] against-them. And-arranged David the-battle to-meet Aram, and-they-fought with-him.

**19:18** And-fled Aram from-before Yisra'el, and-killed David from-Aram seven thousand chariots and-forty thousand foot-soldiers [ish ragli], and-Shofakh the-commander of-the-army he-killed.

**19:19** And-saw the-servants of-Hadad'ezer that they-were-struck before Yisra'el, and-they-made-peace [vayyashlimu] with David and-served-him [vayyaa'vduhu]. And-was-not Aram willing [avah] to-help [lehoshi'a] the-sons of-Ammon again.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — The shaming:** The double humiliation — shaving and cutting garments to expose the buttocks — is an act of diplomatic outrage. The Hebrew *mifsa'ah* (buttocks/seat) makes the exposure explicit. This is a calculated insult to David through his ambassadors.

**v.6 — "a thousand talents of silver":** This detail is unique to Chronicles; 2 Samuel 10 does not mention the payment. The Chronicler emphasizes the scale of the Ammonite military investment.

**v.7 — "thirty-two thousand chariots":** A staggering number. 2 Samuel 10:6 lists "twenty thousand foot soldiers" from Beth-rehob and Zobah, plus smaller contingents. The Chronicler's numbers are characteristically larger.

**v.18 — "seven thousand chariots":** 2 Samuel 10:18 reads "seven hundred chariots." Again, the Chronicler's figures are ten times larger. Whether this reflects textual corruption or deliberate amplification is debated.

*— EMET*
